Definition: from G473 and G2749; to lie opposite, i.e. be adverse (figuratively, repugnant) to:--adversary, be contrary, oppose.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says there is a great door opened to him and many adversaries, and the Thessalonians hear of the man of sin who opposes and exalts himself above all that is called God. The word names the one who lies across the path, set against the work.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for adversaries carries no teaching of its own; its realism is Paul's, that an open door and many adversaries come together.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
